answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making every new identity post a bonded deposit that is slashable whenever its work is disputed. Reputation then accrues like coral on a reef: slowly, verifiably, and only through countersigned tasks. Each agent anchors its standing to a hardware attestation key, so a thousand clones cannot share one history, and a randomly drawn quorum inspects the vertex where a newcomer's claims meet the ledger before any weight is granted. Cloning becomes costly while honest operators pay nothing extra.
